transformations: diagonalized each upstream full inertia tensor into an equivalent principal-frame quaternion and diagonal inertia
omitted visual meshes, the hand, fingers, tendon, gripper actuator, light, and keyframe

replaced source collision meshes with AVBD-authored analytic primitive proxies; the link0 proxy rounds its pinned mesh bounds outward except for clamping the mesh's 32 micrometre lower numerical tail to the mounting plane
expressed the seven supported upstream arm actuators as MJCF motor elements while preserving names, joint bindings, and effort limits

materialized MuJoCo's implicit geom friction tuple explicitly; AVBD currently consumes its sliding coefficient and records the unsupported torsional and rolling coefficients without claiming solver equivalence

semanticDefaults.avbdSupport: The importer consumes the first (sliding) coefficient. Torsional and rolling friction are retained in the source MJCF for provenance but are not implemented by AVBD.

firstPartyPusher.designRationale: An 18 mm diameter provides a robust primitive contact patch on the 40 mm-thick Push-T workpiece. A 110 mm total length centered at a round 200 mm link7 offset reaches the table while retaining proximal overlap with AVBD's link7 proxy. The resulting endpoints make the mount and TCP independently auditable.
firstPartyPusher.massModel: collision-only attachment; the pinned upstream link7 inertial is intentionally unchanged

benchmarkBoundary.statement: No ManiSkill asset data is present in panda_pusher.xml.
benchmarkBoundary.taskStatus: The task intentionally remains a ManiSkill PushT-v1 behavioral port. Its reset pose and distributions, workpiece properties, controller cadence, observation schema, reward, pseudo-render score, and success threshold are benchmark-derived configuration and are not claimed as clean-room AVBD design.
